Based on my research, I can help clarify this historical connection:

**Vladimir Rapoport's Country:** Vladimir Rapoport (1907-1975) was a Soviet cinematographer and film director, making the **Soviet Union** his country of citizenship.

**The World Leader:** **President Harry S. Truman** of the United States frequently characterized the Soviet Union as an imperialist power in the context of the Cold War. He described Communist actions as "imperialist" and stated that the Korean invasion was "very obviously inspired by the Soviet Union."

**Where Truman Announced Intervention:** President Truman announced the U.S. intervention in the Korean War on **June 27, 1950**. The announcement was made from his office at the **White House** (as part of his presidential communications). On this date, he ordered U.S. air and naval forces to South Korea to provide cover and support to Republic of Korea government forces.

In his justification, Truman stated that "communism has passed beyond the use of subversion to conquer independent nations and will now use armed invasion and war," characterizing the conflict as part of a broader fight against "Communist imperialism" that he attributed to Soviet influence.

This announcement marked America's entry into the Korean War, though notably, Truman did not seek a formal declaration of war from Congress, designating the operation as a "police action" under UN Security Council Resolution 83.
